subject: accountancy

concepts.title: Classification of Capital and Revenue Expenditures
concepts.definition: Expenditures that yield enduring advantages across multiple accounting cycles and enhance asset capacity are capital, whereas outlays consumed entirely within the current accounting period to support routine operations are revenue.
concepts.key_idea: Capital outlays provide multi-period benefits and go to the balance sheet, while revenue outlays maintain ongoing business activities and appear in the income statement.
question_patterns: classify the given expenditure as capital or revenue
distinguish whether the expense on ... is capital or revenue
state giving reasons whether the outlay is capital expenditure or revenue expenditure
identify the nature of expenditure for ...
explain classification of capital and revenue expenditures

solution_steps.action: examine the enduring nature and future benefit duration
solution_steps.explain: If the benefit extends beyond one year or increases capacity, it is capital; if it maintains regular operations for the current year, it is revenue.

solution_steps.action: assign appropriate financial statement classification
solution_steps.explain: Capital expenditures are capitalized on the balance sheet subject to depreciation, whereas revenue items are charged to the trading and profit and loss account.

concepts.title: Capital Receipts and Revenue Receipts
concepts.definition: Monetary inflows that establish a future settlement obligation or arise from disposing of long-term assets are capital receipts, whereas inflows generated from ordinary sales and recurring investments are revenue receipts.
concepts.key_idea: Capital receipts create claims or decrease fixed assets, whereas revenue receipts augment routine trading income.
question_patterns: identify whether the given receipt is of capital or revenue nature
classify the cash receipt into capital receipt or revenue receipt
distinguish between capital and revenue receipts for the following items
determine the nature of inflow from ...
explain capital receipts and revenue receipts

solution_steps.action: check for obligation to return or fixed asset disposal
solution_steps.explain: A receipt involving equity, loan liability, or asset sale is a capital receipt; otherwise, it constitutes revenue receipt.

solution_steps.action: place item in position statement or trading and profit and loss account
solution_steps.explain: Capital receipts affect balance sheet equity/liabilities, while revenue receipts appear on the credit side of the income statement.

concepts.title: Computation of Cost of Goods Sold
concepts.definition: Cost of goods sold measures the direct cost of inventory and manufacturing effort incurred to produce the volume of goods actually sold during the accounting period.
concepts.key_idea: Sum opening inventory, purchases net of returns, and direct manufacturing costs, then deduct unsold closing inventory.

solution_steps.explain: Subtract unsold inventory remaining at the end of the year.

concepts.title: Computation of Gross Profit or Gross Loss
concepts.definition: Gross profit represents the surplus of net operational sales over the cost of goods sold, reflecting the direct trading profitability of the enterprise.
concepts.key_idea: Net sales minus the sum of opening inventory, purchases, and direct costs adjusted for closing stock gives gross profit.

concepts.title: Preparation of Trading Account and Closing Entries
concepts.definition: The trading account is the initial segment of the income statement designed to establish direct operational results through ledger closing entries transferring trading items.
concepts.key_idea: Direct manufacturing and acquisition balances are closed to debit of trading account, and sales revenue to credit.
question_patterns: prepare a trading account for the year ended ...

solution_steps.action: debit trading account for direct cost elements
solution_steps.explain: Transfer opening stock, net purchases, freight inwards, wages, and power to the debit of trading account.

solution_steps.action: credit trading account for net revenues and closing stock
solution_steps.explain: Transfer net sales and credit closing inventory to the credit side of trading account.

solution_steps.action: balance the account to find gross profit or gross loss
solution_steps.explain: Transfer resulting gross profit (or gross loss) to profit and loss account.

concepts.title: Computation of Net Profit or Net Loss
concepts.definition: Net profit is the definitive earnings figure of a firm for an accounting year after incorporating all secondary incomes and deducting administrative, selling, financial, and other indirect operating and non-operating expenses from gross profit.
concepts.key_idea: Net profit equals gross profit plus non-trading revenues less all indirect administrative, selling, and general expenses.
question_patterns: calculate net profit from the given profit and loss account balances

solution_steps.action: sum total indirect revenues and gains
solution_steps.explain: Add discount received, commission earned, interest received, and other incomes to gross profit.

solution_steps.action: sum all indirect expenses and losses
solution_steps.explain: Aggregate rent, salaries, advertisement, interest paid, bad debts, depreciation, and repair costs.

solution_steps.action: compute net profit
solution_steps.explain: Subtract total indirect expenses from total income side.

concepts.title: Computation of Operating Profit (EBIT)
concepts.definition: Operating profit measures earnings derived exclusively from the core commercial activities of an enterprise prior to deducting non-operating finance charges and abnormal losses, and before adding extraneous investment gains.
concepts.key_idea: Earnings before interest, taxes, and abnormal events isolate regular operational earnings from financial financing decisions.

solution_steps.action: add non-operating expenses to net profit
solution_steps.explain: Add back interest on loan, loss by fire, and loss on sale of fixed assets to net profit.

solution_steps.explain: Deduct dividend on investment, profit on sale of assets, and non-trading gains.

concepts.title: Computation of Closing Capital in Balance Sheet
concepts.definition: Closing capital represents the proprietor's net residual equity at the end of the period, obtained by augmenting beginning capital with net profit and reducing it by drawings, income tax, and personal withdrawals.
concepts.key_idea: The owner's opening equity increases with annual profits and decreases with personal cash or goods drawings and income tax outlays.
question_patterns: calculate closing capital to be shown in the balance sheet

solution_steps.action: add net profit to opening capital
solution_steps.explain: The annual net earnings are credited to the owner's capital account.

solution_steps.action: deduct drawings and personal tax payments
solution_steps.explain: Drawings and personal income tax payments reduce the proprietor's capital.

concepts.title: Marshalling and Grouping of Balance Sheet Items
concepts.definition: Marshalling is the systematic sequence of presenting assets and liabilities in the position statement under either the order of permanence or the order of liquidity, grouped under appropriate category headings.
concepts.key_idea: Order of permanence lists least convertible assets and owner's equity first, whereas order of liquidity starts with cash and short-term debt.
question_patterns: explain grouping and marshalling of assets and liabilities

solution_steps.action: classify items into current and non-current groups
solution_steps.explain: Categorize accounts into current assets, fixed assets, current liabilities, long-term debts, and capital.

solution_steps.action: order accounts by selected marshalling method
solution_steps.explain: For permanence, arrange from fixed/permanent to liquid; for liquidity, list cash and immediate obligations first.

concepts.title: Recording the Opening Journal Entry
concepts.definition: An opening journal entry is passed on the first day of an accounting period to record the carried-forward balances of assets, liabilities, and proprietor's capital from the prior year's balance sheet.
concepts.key_idea: All individual asset accounts are debited, while liability accounts and owner's capital account are credited.
question_patterns: record the opening journal entry for the next accounting year

explain recording the opening journal entry

solution_steps.action: debit individual asset accounts
solution_steps.explain: Debit all real and personal accounts possessing debit balances carried forward from the balance sheet.

solution_steps.action: credit individual liability and capital accounts
solution_steps.explain: Credit all external obligations and owner's net equity to maintain double-entry equality.
